g.text: With private parking added: the corridor, area by area

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Blue: modelled automobiles (90 % interval). Orange: places of the legal curb at 5.37 m (upper bound). Green: curb plus the private places

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: of buildings of five dwellings or fewer, counting only places a car can leave without another being moved (90 % interval).

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Every lot was read on aerial imagery; the estimate is calibrated on 99 lots judged by the author from street-level imagery.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Corridor: 4,622 modelled automobiles; 6,930 curb places; 9,158 with 2,228 private places (2,051–2,414). Not counted: garage interiors,

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: and the parking of the 96 buildings of six dwellings or more (2,592 dwellings), several of which have an underground garage.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Sources: SAAQ, vehicles released under the access Act (file 03.06.34729), December 31, 2024, type inferred; Statistics Canada, 2021 Census;

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: City of Montréal, géobase, parking-sign inventory and assessment roll (CC BY 4.0). Automobiles below the FSA are MODELLED, not measured.
